subject: Provisioned ramp breakpoint & soft-exit approval request — Pharos Health
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@pharoshealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Provisioned ramp breakpoint & soft-exit approval request — Pharos Health

Elena — thanks again for the time this morning. As discussed, Pharos is comfortable committing to a 12-month pilot but would like: (1) a staged ramp (provisioned breakpoints at months 3 and 6) with the ability to downscale to a smaller committed bucket at month 6 without full termination, and (2) a limited opt-out window after month 3 in case the clinical POC materially misses acceptance criteria.

To keep the team aligned, here's what I'm proposing for the deal desk / exec review:
- Ramp schedule: 25% of committed capacity months 0–3 (pilot onboarding), 60% months 4–6, 100% months 7–12.
- Downsell protection: at month 6 Pharos can elect a single downsizing to 50% of remaining commitment. If exercised, we provide a pro-rated credit equal to unused committed capacity converted at 60% list to be applied as account credits or applied to the final invoice.
- Soft-exit opt-out: after month 3 Pharos may terminate with 45 days' notice; termination triggers the downsell-credit path (not full refund). No early termination charge beyond the pro-rated credit.

These are non-standard vs our playbook (discount + opt-out + downsell credit) so we need deal desk / exec sign-off. I attached the current statement-of-work with the redline (PH-Statement-v3-redline.pdf).

Next steps: can Marissa / Karthik confirm whether we need an exec waiver for the pricing/credit cap and any guardrails legal will require? Elena — if this looks directionally right, happy to have your counsel loop in for a short redline pass.

— Soojin

Thanks Soojin — looping in deal desk to evaluate. Quick questions before we escalate to execs:
1) Confirm total committed ARR (list price) in the SOW and the implied discount to list if we apply the 60% conversion factor for unused capacity.
2) Is Pharos asking for a single-use downsell option (one-time at month 6) or unlimited? Your note says single — I want that explicit in the commercial term.
3) Any requests for data retention / audit logs beyond our standard eDiscovery + audit log offering? Legal will flag.

Tentative recommendation from deal desk: we can approve the ramp breakpoints + single-use downsell credit in principle but we need an exec sign-off for any arrangement that: (a) exposes us to >$75k in gross credits (financial cap), or (b) creates an opt-out earlier than month 6.

I attached the deal sheet summary (deal-sheet-PR-894.pdf) with a pro-forma credit exposure calc. If this stays below $75k cap and Pharos accepts single-use, suggest routing to Markus for sign-off with these guardrails.

— Marissa Cole
Senior Deal Desk Manager | Redwood Inference

Markus — forwarding for exec review. TL;DR: Pharos (strategic healthcare POC) is requesting a non-standard ramp/soft-exit construct: staged ramp (3/6/12), one-time downsell at month 6 with a 60% conversion-to-credit on unused committed capacity, and a 45-day opt-out after month 3.

Why this matters: Pharos is a reference target in our healthcare vertical — high technical fit and potential multi-product expansion. The credit exposure (Marissa's pro-forma) shows a worst-case hit of ~$92k if Pharos fully downscales at month 6 and reduces consumption. Deal desk recommends approval if we impose a hard credit cap of $100k, require a single-use downsell election, and tie the soft-exit to verification of POC acceptance criteria (so the opt-out is only available if acceptance criteria are not met).

Legal notes: we need to ensure the SOW defines the acceptance criteria clearly and that the credit application is limited to Redwood-hosted invoices (no cash refunds), and we should preserve audit rights. Also propose we keep the pricing/discount confidential per standard practice.

Requested action: Can you review and either (a) approve with the deal desk conditions (cap: $100k, single-use downsell, acceptance-criteria gating), or (b) request alternate guardrails.

Quoted message (original Soojin email) included below.

Karthik / Marissa / Soojin — reviewed. Approve with conditions below: 

1) Credit cap: cap total applied credits to account at $100,000 maximum (no cash refunds).
2) Single downsell election: Pharos allowed one downsizing election at the month-6 breakpoint only; election must be submitted in writing 14 days prior to the month-6 anniversary and will be applied pro-rata per SOW.
3) Acceptance gating: Soft-exit opt-out is available only if Pharos fails to meet the mutually agreed POC acceptance criteria documented in SOW Exhibit A. If acceptance criteria are met, opt-out is void and standard early-termination charges apply.
4) Visibility & pilot metrics: require weekly onboarding check-ins weeks 1–12 and a metrics packet at month 3 to validate acceptance gating.

Soojin — please incorporate these conditions into the SOW redline and route to Pharos' counsel for a narrow acceptance gating clause and to Legal for a confidentiality carve. Once legal confirms, you have my sign-off to execute.

— Markus Klein
